speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that summary; it is quite complex. To begin our investigation, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as blurred vision or double vision? Also, could you describe the specific nature of your gait difficulty—is it unsteady, scissoring, or do you feel like you are being pulled to one side?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That "drunk" appearance suggests a cerebellar issue; could you tell me if your difficulty with balance has been present since you first noticed the vision changes, or did the ataxia start later? Also, do you experience any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs besides the clumsiness?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with and without contrast.
REQUEST TEST: JC Virus antibody index.
